benchmark.category: a mini BigBasket-style online grocery store with a delivery-partner app and an admin console
benchmark.users: Indian households ordering groceries, fruits and staples online, delivery riders fulfilling assigned orders from a phone, and store admins managing catalogue, orders and partner approvals

requirements.source_phrase: it has all the grocery items and fruits and all the items related to bigbasket items
requirements.statement: /shop lists every seeded grocery, fruit and staple product with its name, unit, price and image, and the home page shows category tiles that open the matching filtered listing
requirements.notes: Home and /shop are the first two surfaces a shopper meets; each category tile must open /shop filtered to that category, not a dead link.

requirements.source_phrase: it has all the grocery items and fruits and all the items related to bigbasket items
requirements.statement: GET /api/products returns every product in the store with id, name, unit, price, mrp, image, category and stock, a category parameter returns only that category, and GET /api/products/{id} returns that one product
requirements.notes: The catalogue must come from the store, not a hard-coded list in the frontend bundle.

requirements.statement: A fresh database starts with exactly 46 seeded grocery products spread across the category tiles, each with a non-zero price, a unit and stock, and restarting the backend creates no duplicate rows
requirements.notes: Build description: '46 products seeded on startup if products collection empty'. The count is the developer's, so it is checked for a non-empty consistent seed (no duplicates) rather than as a user-given value.

requirements.source_phrase: it should include 40 rupees as the delivery charge
requirements.statement: POST /api/orders/checkout and every stored order set delivery_fee to exactly 40 and total to subtotal plus 40, whatever the cart size or a client-supplied delivery_fee says
requirements.notes: Numeric rule: total = sum(price x qty) + 40, in whole rupees; inputs are stored product price and cart quantity. The fee has no threshold, no waiver and no doubling on one order.

requirements.source_phrase: it should include 40 rupees as the delivery charge
requirements.statement: The cart sheet and /cart show a delivery line of 40 rupees and a grand total equal to the sum of line totals plus 40, in whole rupees
requirements.notes: The displayed total must equal the stored total the backend computes, to the rupee.

requirements.source_phrase: for deliver ppl and for admins
requirements.statement: Every signed-in account carries exactly one of customer, delivery or admin, and the header shows the admin console link only to an admin and the delivery dashboard link only to a delivery partner
requirements.notes: Hiding the link is not enforcement; the matching backend refusals are written separately.

requirements.source_phrase: for deliver ppl and for admins
requirements.statement: GET /api/me with a valid Clerk session returns the caller's id, name, email and role, and without a token returns 401 with no user field
requirements.notes: Role is the single value the frontend guards and the server enforces read from.

requirements.statement: /sign-in and /sign-up render working Clerk email-and-password forms, and a successful sign-in returns the user to the storefront signed in
requirements.notes: Email plus password is the only credential path the user chose; no social login is promised.

requirements.statement: A Clerk session token minted for a seeded account authenticates GET /api/me and the role-scoped endpoints, while a missing or invalid token returns 401 with no user data
requirements.notes: Clerk bot protection blocks automated sign-in with passwords, so Phase 4 uses a minted session token or a sign-in ticket as the build description describes.

requirements.source_phrase: **the website should not contain  pay on deliver r a cash on delivery only prepayment**
requirements.statement: The cart and checkout screens offer only online prepaid payment: no cash-on-delivery or pay-on-delivery option, button or copy appears anywhere in the buying flow
requirements.notes: The user's line is emphatic; the UI test also checks the string does not reappear in a help or FAQ block.

requirements.source_phrase: **the website should not contain  pay on deliver r a cash on delivery only prepayment**
requirements.statement: POST /api/orders/checkout refuses a request naming any payment method other than online Razorpay and creates no order for it
requirements.notes: Prepaid-only must hold on the API path, not just be hidden in the screen.

requirements.statement: The checkout payment step creates its charge through Razorpay using a key read on the server, and the resulting order records the Razorpay order id and payment id the provider returns
requirements.notes: Keys were skipped, so the configured path is verified as written and the unconfigured path is checked separately.

requirements.statement: With no Razorpay keys in the environment, POST /api/orders/checkout returns 503 saying online payments are not configured and creates no order and no charge
requirements.notes: The user skipped the key question; the build description states the 503 contract. The test asserts no order document is written on this path.

requirements.statement: When checkout answers 503 for missing payment configuration the cart screen shows that message as a toast or inline error and stays usable, with no crash and no empty confirmation screen
requirements.notes: Build description: 'the UI should toast it (no crash)'.

requirements.statement: A signed-in shopper sees a floating 'Ask AI' button outside /admin, /delivery and the sign-in pages; opening it streams a reply in the chat sheet and the conversation is still there after a reload
requirements.notes: Two AI surfaces were chosen; this one is the shopper-facing chat.

requirements.statement: POST /api/ai/chat streams the assistant's reply as SSE for the signed-in user, GET /api/ai/chat/history returns that user's messages in order, and a clear request empties only that user's history
requirements.notes: Streaming must end with the full text, not a truncated buffer.

requirements.statement: A signed-out visitor who opens the AI button is prompted to sign in and no AI request is sent
requirements.notes: Build description: the floating button is visible while signed out and shows a sign-in prompt; the chat itself requires a user for per-user history.

requirements.statement: The chat and insights endpoints call the Claude Sonnet 5.5 model with the injected key and return its content; a missing key or provider error comes back as an error the screen can show, never an empty string or a canned reply
requirements.notes: The model is named by the user; the response must change with the input rather than being a fixed placeholder.

requirements.source_phrase: it should include 40 rupees as the delivery charge
requirements.statement: Asked about delivery or payment, the assistant's reply states a 40 rupee delivery charge and that only prepaid online payment is accepted with no cash on delivery
requirements.notes: Grounded in both the delivery-charge line and the no-COD line; the assistant must not invent a different fee or offer cash on delivery.

requirements.statement: The /admin overview has a 'Generate insights' control that streams sales-insight text into the page for the signed-in admin
requirements.notes: Admin-only surface; a customer must not reach it.

requirements.statement: POST /api/admin/ai/insights streams insights grounded in the store's order data for an admin token and returns 403 for a customer token
requirements.notes: The 403 is the server-side half of the admin-only insights rule.

requirements.statement: A signed-in customer can open /partner, submit the delivery-partner application and then see an 'under review' state instead of the form
requirements.notes: The application is made from inside the app by an existing signed-in user.

requirements.statement: POST /api/delivery/apply stores the application against the caller with a pending status and leaves the caller's role customer; a second pending application from the same user is refused
requirements.notes: Refusing the duplicate is the paranoid half of the signup promise.

requirements.statement: An admin approving an application sets that user's role to delivery so GET /api/me reports delivery on the next request, while rejecting keeps the role customer and stores the admin's note
requirements.notes: Self-signup creates the request; only an admin grants the role.

requirements.statement: /admin/partners lists pending applications and lets the admin approve or reject each one with a note, and the row updates to the new state
requirements.notes: The control must change its own state and the applicant's visible status.

requirements.source_phrase: for deliver ppl and for admins
requirements.statement: /admin opens an overview with order and revenue KPIs and a low-stock panel, and reaches /admin/products, /admin/orders, /admin/partners and /admin/users
requirements.notes: The admin half of the three-role promise.

requirements.source_phrase: for deliver ppl and for admins
requirements.statement: GET /api/admin/overview returns the store's counts and revenue totals for an admin token, and every /api/admin/* endpoint returns 403 for a customer token and 401 without a token
requirements.notes: Direct requests with a customer token must be refused, not merely unreachable from the UI.

requirements.statement: /delivery lists the orders assigned to the signed-in rider with their status, and the rider can advance an assigned order to out-for-delivery and then delivered
requirements.notes: The rider's two-step advance is the core delivery control.

requirements.statement: GET /api/delivery/orders returns only orders assigned to the calling rider, and PATCH advances an assigned order through out_for_delivery and delivered with a timeline entry per step
requirements.notes: Scoping to the assigned rider is checked separately as an isolation requirement.

requirements.statement: Every failed action in the UI shows a plain-language message naming what went wrong and what to do next, and never a stack trace, a raw provider error or a secret
requirements.notes: 'Clear' is made testable as the readable failure path of every action.

requirements.statement: Every API error response carries a human-readable message in the same shape across endpoints and leaks no stack trace, key or token
requirements.notes: The screen can only show a good message if the API sends one in a consistent field.

requirements.statement: A second sign-up with an email already registered is refused and creates no second account or user document
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of the signup promise: the second identical record must be refused.

requirements.statement: After signing out the protected pages redirect to /sign-in and the app makes no further signed-in API call with the old session
requirements.notes: Inverse of the session promise; observed in the network panel after sign-out.

requirements.statement: A Clerk session token invalidated by sign-out is refused by /api/me and every role-scoped endpoint with 401 and returns no data
requirements.notes: A frontend redirect alone is not a sign-out if the token still works on the API.

requirements.statement: Items added to the cart survive a page reload in the same browser with their quantities, and the header cart count matches the number of items restored
requirements.notes: Build description: the cart lives in localStorage per browser; the test reloads rather than reopening a new session.

requirements.statement: The restored cart's prices and stock come from GET /api/products at page load, so a product price changed in the admin console shows the new price in the cart
requirements.notes: A stale localStorage price must never be the price charged.

requirements.statement: The add-to-cart stepper stops at the lower of the product's stock and 20 and shows that limit instead of silently accepting more
requirements.notes: Build description: max min(stock,20). The cap is a frontend guard; the server re-checks stock.

requirements.statement: POST /api/orders/checkout refuses a line whose quantity exceeds the product's current stock and creates no order
requirements.notes: Two submissions arriving together must not both pass the stock check for the same last unit.

requirements.statement: The cart sheet and /cart with nothing in the cart show an explicit empty message with a link back to /shop and a disabled pay button, not a blank panel or a spinner
requirements.notes: Empty state of the primary money screen.

requirements.statement: A checkout request with an empty item list is refused with a readable message and creates no order
requirements.notes: No zero-rupee order may be written.

requirements.statement: /shop with a search or category that matches nothing shows an explicit no-products message and keeps the search box usable
requirements.notes: Empty state of the listing surface the user asked for.

requirements.statement: GET /api/products with a query matching nothing returns an empty list with 200, not an error and not the full catalogue
requirements.notes: A search that silently falls back to everything would look like a match.

requirements.statement: A product with zero stock still opens at /product/:id, shows out of stock and disables add to cart
requirements.notes: Boundary value of the stock rule.

requirements.statement: GET /api/products/{id} returns stock 0 for an out-of-stock product and checkout refuses any line for it
requirements.notes: Disabled button and refused request are both required.

requirements.statement: Checkout refuses to submit an address unless the phone is a 10-digit Indian mobile starting 6-9 and the pincode is 6 digits, and marks the offending field
requirements.notes: Build description names these rules; the delivery address is what makes the order deliverable.

requirements.statement: POST /api/orders/checkout refuses an address whose phone is not 10 digits starting 6-9 or whose pincode is not 6 digits, and creates no order
requirements.notes: Validation must hold on the API path, not only in the form.

requirements.statement: POST /api/orders/checkout recomputes every line total from the stored product price and quantity and ignores any price the client sends, so the order total matches the catalogue
requirements.notes: Protects the money rule from a tampered browser cart.

requirements.statement: A signed-in customer requesting GET /api/orders/{id} for an order belonging to another customer is refused with 404 and receives no field of that order
requirements.notes: Guessed identifier from outside the account; the user's 'secure' line covers this.

requirements.statement: A rider PATCHing an order not assigned to them is refused and the order's status and timeline are unchanged
requirements.notes: The least-privileged role must not reach a privileged action by direct request.

requirements.statement: An admin changing another user's role takes effect on that user's next request, and demoting the last remaining admin is refused so at least one admin always exists
requirements.notes: Build description: cannot demote last admin.

requirements.statement: Removing a product in /admin removes it from GET /api/products and the storefront while orders that already contain it keep their stored line
requirements.notes: Deleting history with the catalogue item would corrupt past order totals.

requirements.statement: An admin cancelling an order returns each line's quantity to its product's stock exactly once, and cancelling the same order again is refused
requirements.notes: Idempotency of a stock-mutating action.

requirements.statement: An order moves placed, packed, out_for_delivery, delivered with a timeline entry per step, and a step taken out of order or by the wrong role is refused
requirements.notes: Build description gives the lifecycle; only the allowed transitions may succeed.

requirements.statement: The customer's /orders/:id shows the order's status and every timeline entry with its time, and it updates after the rider marks the order delivered
requirements.notes: The customer must see the same transitions the rider performs.

requirements.statement: POST /api/orders/{id}/verify with a bad Razorpay signature fails and leaves the order unpaid, while a valid signature marks it paid once
requirements.notes: Build description: a bad signature must not pay an order.

requirements.statement: GET /api/ai/chat/history returns only the calling user's messages, and a request naming another user's history id returns nothing of it
requirements.notes: Per-user chat history is a private record; a guessed id must be refused.

requirements.statement: Every order's total equals the sum of its line totals plus the 40 rupee delivery fee, and each line total equals the stored unit price times quantity, in whole rupees
requirements.notes: Formula: line_total = price x qty; subtotal = sum(line_total); total = subtotal + 40. Inputs are stored prices; no rounding beyond whole rupees is expected.

requirements.statement: A paid order decrements each product's stock exactly once by its ordered quantity, and a replayed verify or webhook does not decrement it again
requirements.notes: The provider may deliver the same confirmation twice; stock must not move twice.

requirements.statement: The /admin overview order count, revenue total and pending count equal the corresponding aggregates of the store's orders for the period shown
requirements.notes: Every displayed aggregate must equal the rows it counts; cancelled and unpaid orders are excluded by the rule the app states on screen.

requirements.statement: The 7-day revenue chart plots one value per day equal to the sum of that day's paid order totals and shows zero for a day with no orders
requirements.notes: Dates follow the store's day boundary; a missing day must render as zero, not be skipped.

requirements.statement: The low-stock panel lists exactly the products whose stock sits below the panel's stated threshold and shows each one's current stored stock
requirements.notes: The threshold used by the query and the label on screen must agree.

requirements.statement: The storefront, product detail, cart and checkout keep their primary content and controls visible without overlap or horizontal scrolling at 375px and 1440px widths
requirements.notes: A grocery shopper is mostly on a phone; the mobile bottom cart bar is part of this check.

requirements.statement: Body and button text meets a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background on every screen the app ships
requirements.notes: Measured on the rendered page with the shipped theme.

requirements.statement: Adding to cart changes the button to a quantity stepper and updates the header cart count in the same interaction, with no silent success
requirements.notes: Every action answers on screen; the control itself changes state.

requirements.statement: A product whose image URL is broken or empty renders a placeholder at the same size as a real product image instead of a blank gap
requirements.notes: Catalogue images come from URLs an admin enters; a bad URL is expected.

requirements.statement: Opening /admin/products or /admin/orders directly as a signed-in admin renders the page with its data, and a reload keeps the admin there
requirements.notes: Every screen renders from a deep link without a blank page.

requirements.statement: The /shop search query, category and sort are reflected in the URL so a reload and the back button restore the same filtered, sorted list
requirements.notes: Filters survive reload and back-navigation and reset when cleared.

requirements.statement: Loading, disabled and error states on the product, cart and admin tables look different from the populated state, and a failed fetch shows an error rather than an empty table
requirements.notes: An error rendered as an empty list reads as real zero rows.

requirements.statement: A signed-out visitor opening /orders, /admin or /delivery is sent to /sign-in rather than seeing a blank page or a broken shell
requirements.notes: Protected page while signed out redirects to auth.

requirements.statement: A customer whose delivery application is still pending cannot open /delivery and is shown their application status instead of the dashboard
requirements.notes: Approval gates the dashboard; the weeks before approval must not leak it.

requirements.statement: No response body, page source or client bundle contains the Clerk secret, the Razorpay key secret or the model key
requirements.notes: The user asked for a secure site; secrets stay on the server.

requirements.statement: The /admin/products add dialog validates its fields, including MRP greater than or equal to price, and the new product appears in the admin list and on the storefront after saving
requirements.notes: Build description names the MRP rule; the admin must be able to stock the store the shopper browses.

requirements.statement: POST /api/products with an admin token stores the product and GET /api/products returns it, while a payload with MRP below price or a missing name is refused and stores nothing
requirements.notes: Validation holds on the API path as well as the dialog.

requirements.statement: An order created at checkout reads back with the same items, address, totals and status from GET /api/orders in a new session for its owner
requirements.notes: Persisted, not held in browser state; read back from a fresh session.

requirements.statement: Every order receives a distinct order_number, and two orders created at the same moment do not share one
requirements.notes: A unique value enforced by the store, not by a read-then-write race.

requirements.statement: GET /api/products returns every matching product exactly once across its pages, and its total count equals the rows it returns
requirements.notes: Checked with a page size smaller than the seeded catalogue.

requirements.statement: An admin-entered product image URL is stored and served back on the product detail and listing pages as the same URL the admin saved
requirements.notes: The field the dialog sends is a field the API stores and returns.

requirements.statement: The assistant's streamed reply renders completely in the chat sheet, ends with the full text, and product tags render as chips with a working Add button
requirements.notes: A stream that stops mid-sentence is a visible defect; a chip that does nothing is a dead control.

requirements.statement: The assistant returns different, on-topic replies for different shopping questions and never the same fixed placeholder for every input
requirements.notes: Checked with two known inputs whose right answers differ in content.

requirements.statement: Generated sales insights name figures that match the store's actual order data for the period and invent no product or revenue total the data lacks
requirements.notes: The admin acts on these numbers; a fabricated total is worse than no insight.

requirements.statement: When the AI provider fails or its key is missing the chat sheet shows an error message and stays usable, never an empty bubble or a fake reply
requirements.notes: Provider errors surface to the user in their terms.

requirements.statement: The Razorpay order created at checkout carries the same amount in paise as the order total shown on screen, and one checkout produces exactly one Razorpay order
requirements.notes: Server computes the charged amount; the screen must show the same figure.

requirements.statement: A declined or abandoned Razorpay payment creates no paid order and grants no order status beyond unpaid, and the customer sees the failure
requirements.notes: Prepaid only: nothing ships on an unpaid order.

requirements.statement: After a successful payment the customer lands on an order confirmation showing the order number, items and total, and the order appears in /orders
requirements.notes: Product-shell surface every checkout has; no success without a stored order.

requirements.statement: Every /api route that reads user data validates the Clerk session token on the server and derives the user id from it, never from a request-supplied id
requirements.notes: A user_id query parameter must not be trusted for identity.

requirements.statement: The Razorpay key id and secret are read on the server from the environment, and only the key id reaches the browser
requirements.notes: A missing or placeholder key fails the checkout path with the 503 the user's skip established.

requirements.statement: Opening and closing the AI chat repeatedly keeps one active stream at a time, delivers each reply once and leaves no duplicated message in the history
requirements.notes: Repeated open/close must not stack SSE connections or duplicate messages.

requirements.statement: GET /api/products and the admin order list answer in about the same time with a thousand rows as with a handful by paging rather than returning everything
requirements.notes: Large collection loads by page.

requirements.statement: Every route the navigation reaches (/, /shop, /product/:id, /cart, /orders, /partner, /admin, /admin/products, /admin/orders, /admin/users, /delivery, /sign-in, /sign-up) loads without a build error, undefined name or blank screen
requirements.notes: Build and deployment class: the deployed app behaves as the preview does.

requirements.statement: The backend builds its API base and every third-party client from environment variables and contains no hard-coded host, key or port
requirements.notes: The frontend reads its backend base from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL per the build description.

requirements.statement: Typing 'aloo' or a Hindi product tag in the /shop search returns the matching potato products, and typing the English product name returns the same product
requirements.notes: benchmark: grocery storefronts -- search matches regional and Hindi names as well as English ones, which the seeded Hindi tags exist for

requirements.statement: GET /api/products with q matches product names and their Hindi tags case-insensitively and returns only the matching products
requirements.notes: benchmark: grocery storefronts -- search over the catalogue, not a client-side filter of one page

requirements.statement: The /shop sort select reorders the visible list by price low-to-high, price high-to-low and name, and the visible order matches the values shown on the cards
requirements.notes: benchmark: grocery storefronts -- a sort control every shopper expects next to the filter

requirements.statement: GET /api/products with a sort parameter returns the rows ordered by that field consistently, with equal values kept in a stable order across pages
requirements.notes: benchmark: grocery storefronts -- sort applies to the whole result set, not the first page

requirements.statement: The product detail page shows the product's price, MRP, unit and stock plus a related-products rail of items from the same category that each open their own detail page
requirements.notes: benchmark: grocery storefronts -- a product page with a related rail is what every catalogue shopper uses to cross-sell

requirements.statement: GET /api/products/{id} returns the product with its category, and the related list returns other products in the same category excluding the product itself
requirements.notes: benchmark: grocery storefronts -- related products come from the catalogue, not a static list

requirements.statement: The home page shows its hero, the category tiles and the deals, fresh and dairy rails, each rail holding real products that open their detail pages
requirements.notes: benchmark: grocery storefronts -- a merchandised home with category tiles and product rails is the entry screen of every BigBasket-style store

requirements.statement: The header cart button shows the number of items in the cart and updates as quantities change, and the mobile bottom cart bar shows the running total
requirements.notes: benchmark: grocery storefronts -- a persistent cart count and running total on mobile

requirements.statement: /orders lists the signed-in customer's own orders newest first with order number, date, total and status, and each row opens its detail
requirements.notes: benchmark: grocery storefronts -- an order history with live status is the reason a shopper returns to the account page

unmapped_phrases.phrase: it should be official like all users
unmapped_phrases.reason: 'official' has no objective specification; the role requirements, the branding and the product-shell requirements carry its testable parts
